proposals.rationale: Extended one methoxyethoxy chain to a diethylene glycol ether to add an additional H-bond acceptor/oxygen, improving aqueous solubility while retaining the core pharmacophore.
Replaced one methyl ether terminus with a free hydroxyl (diol-like side chain) to increase polarity and solubility without altering ring system or synthetic route significantly.
Substituted one methoxyethoxy chain with a dimethylaminoethoxy group, introducing a basic amine to enable salt formation and improve solubility.
Replaced one terminal methyl ether with a morpholine-capped ethoxy chain, adding a basic, water-solubilizing morpholine ring, a common EGFR-inhibitor solubilizing motif.
Simplified one side chain back to a simple methoxy group, reducing molecular weight and synthetic complexity (fewer steps, cheaper building blocks) while keeping one solubilizing ether.
Capped one chain terminus with morpholine via an extra ethylene spacer, combining enhanced solubility with manageable synthetic accessibility (standard amine alkylation).
Moved the alkyne substituent from meta to para on the aniline ring, a simple regiochemical change to probe SAR while keeping identical physicochemical profile and synthetic ease.
Added a fluorine ortho to the aniline nitrogen to modestly modulate electronics/metabolic stability with minimal synthetic complexity increase.
Extended only one side chain to a longer PEG-like diether, increasing solubility while leaving the other arm and synthetic route largely unchanged for straightforward synthesis.
Converted both methyl ethers to free hydroxyls (bis-diol), maximizing polar surface area and solubility while retaining a synthetically accessible quinazoline core.
